name: Eritrean Zigni
description: Zigni, Eritrea's national dish, shares real roots with Ethiopian kai wat, but real Eritrean technique cooks the onions slowly IN oil from the start (not dry, unlike Ethiopian doro wat's technique) for a full hour or more until reddish-brown and jam-like, and finishes with a real splash of vinegar for tang - Eritreans also genuinely use less butter than their Ethiopian neighbors, giving zigni a slightly lighter character.
steps_detailed: Cook the onion in the oil over medium-low heat, stirring often, 45-60 minutes, until it turns reddish-brown and jam-like - real technique keeps the oil in from the start here, unlike Ethiopian doro wat's dry-onion method.
Add the garlic and berbere, and cook 2 minutes until fragrant.
Add the beef and brown, 6-7 minutes.
Add the tomatoes and simmer 35-40 minutes until the beef is tender.
Stir in the vinegar and cilantro just before serving.

name: Eritrean Tihlo
description: Tihlo, unfilled barley dumpling balls dipped into a spicy meat stew, is a genuinely distinct Eritrean specialty, real technique using real barley flour, which isn't a distinct item here, so all-purpose flour stands in for a similarly firm, dippable dumpling.
steps_detailed: Mix the flour and salt with hot water into a firm, smooth dough. Shape into small balls.
Boil the dumpling balls 8-10 minutes until firm and cooked through.
Brown the beef, add the berbere and tomatoes, and simmer 15-18 minutes into a spicy stew.
Serve the dumpling balls alongside the stew for dipping.

name: Eritrean Hilbet
description: Hilbet, a smooth cream made from fenugreek, lentils, and fava beans, is a genuine Eritrean vegan staple, traditionally served with silsi, a berbere-spiced tomato sauce, on top.
steps_detailed: Simmer the lentils and fava beans together in 2 cups water 20-22 minutes until completely soft.
Blend until completely smooth.
Separately, cook the garlic and berbere in a little oil 1 minute, add the tomatoes, and simmer 10-12 minutes into silsi.
Spread the lentil-fava cream on a plate and top with the silsi.

name: Eritrean Alicha
description: Alicha, a mild, non-berbere vegetable stew, is a genuine Eritrean staple, real turmeric giving it a golden color as a real, deliberate contrast to the fiery berbere-based dishes.
steps_detailed: Cook the garlic in a little oil 30 seconds, then add the turmeric and cook 30 seconds more.
Add the potato, green beans, carrot, and bell pepper with a splash of water, and simmer 20-22 minutes until tender.

name: Eritrean Injera
description: Injera, a spongy, fermented flatbread, is shared with Ethiopia and serves as the utensil, plate, and side for Eritrean meals alike, real technique fermenting the batter for real sourness.
steps_detailed: Whisk the teff flour, all-purpose flour, vinegar, and 1 cup water into a thin, smooth batter.
Let sit at room temperature at least 8 hours, ideally 24, to develop real tang.
Pour a thin layer into a hot, lightly oiled non-stick pan and cook, covered, without flipping, 2-3 minutes, until bubbles cover the surface.

name: Eritrean Zigni-Style Pasta
description: Zigni served over pasta rather than injera genuinely reflects Eritrea's real Italian colonial history - this real fusion, distinct from Ethiopian tradition, is a beloved everyday Eritrean meal.
steps_detailed: Cook the onion in a little oil, 15-18 minutes, until deeply softened and reddish-brown.
Add the beef and berbere, and brown, 6-7 minutes.
Add the tomatoes and simmer 20-22 minutes.
Cook the pasta separately per package directions and serve the zigni sauce over it.

name: Eritrean Tsebhi Dorho
description: Tsebhi dorho (dorho), a spicy berbere chicken stew, closely related to Ethiopian doro wat, real Eritrean technique using real slow-cooked onions in oil from the start.
steps_detailed: Cook the onion in the oil, 40-45 minutes, until reddish-brown and jam-like.
Add the garlic and berbere, and cook 2 minutes.
Add the chicken and a splash of water, and simmer 25-28 minutes until tender.
Add the whole hard-boiled egg in the last 10 minutes to soak up the sauce.

name: Eritrean Grilled Fish
description: Grilled fish rubbed with garlic and lemon, reflecting Eritrea's real Red Sea coastal fishing tradition.

Grill or broil, 4-5 minutes per side, until just cooked through.
